feeds.title: ECOgardener Gardening Blog
feeds.description: I'm Dave. I founded ECOgardener in 2015 in hopes of encouraging generations of growers to keep planting. Here at ECOgardener, we educate and provide tools for beginner and seasoned gardeners alike. Ours are efficient, trusted, and long-lasting no matter the size, space or weather.

feeds.title: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center
feeds.description: Explore Texas native plants in our sustainable gardens and arboretum and through our educational programs. The Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center in Austin, Texas, is dedicated to inspiring the conservation of native plants.

feeds.title: Williamson County Chapter
feeds.description: The Native Plant Society of Texas is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporation supported by grants, donations, and member dues. NPSOT's mission is to promote research, conservation, and utilization of native plants and plant habitats of Texas through education, outreach, and example.

feeds.title: Digging
feeds.description: Hello! I'm Pam Penick, a dirt-under-my-nails, hoping-for-rain, spiky-plant lover gardening under the Death Star in Austin, Texas (zone 8b). Here's where I share all the gardening goodness I can dig up, not just at home but wherever I go. Digging is for anyone who loves gardens, a sense of connectedness with nature, real-life plant info, design insights, how-to gardening tips, photos of beautiful plants, and virtual garden tours. D

feeds.title: Gill Garden Center + Landscape Co.
feeds.description: Grow your very best garden with our garden tips, guides, and videos, written by us and our staff for gardens in our area. In 1978, Sally Munroe and James Gill joined as partners to design and install residential and commercial landscapes in the Corpus Christi area. They soon consolidated their partnership by marriage and moved their growing landscape business out of their backyard.

feeds.title: AgriLife Today » Lawn & Garden
feeds.description: this section features articles on Lawn & Garden. The Texas A&M AgriLife strives to improve lives, environments and the Texas economy through education, research, extension and service.

feeds.title: Rainbow Gardens Blog
feeds.description: You've got plant questions, and we've got plant answers. Check out the Happy Gardner blog for tips and tricks to help your garden flourish! Rainbow Gardens has become one of San Antonio's leading garden centers.

feeds.title: Backbone Valley Nursery Blog
feeds.description: Established in 1999, Backbone Valley Nursery is family-owned by the Robertson and Martin families. Our family takes pride in what we do and we strive to provide the very best plants, products, and services in the Highland Lakes area. Backbone started as a wholesale tree nursery and has grown to a full-service garden center and tree farm that offers complete landscape design and installation.

feeds.title: My Garden My Refuge Blog
feeds.description: Hello, I'm Tilelli. I am a proud mother of four, two girls and two boys. I consider myself an accidental gardener, as eight years ago. My new goal is to join the force and convince more people to grow some of their food.

feeds.title: Dallas Garden Buzz
feeds.description: A blog on gardening and recipes planned by gardening experts. They offer residents of Dallas county a chance to see what grows well in Dallas' climate, clay soil, and restricted water.

feeds.title: Premier Nursery Blog
feeds.description: Welcome to Premier Nursery, where affordable landscaping begins. We are a family-owned company with four convenient locations across Tarrant County. Officially opened in 1983, after 34 years in business, our goal is still to provide quality plant material at competitive prices.

feeds.title: My Gardener Says…
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Tina Huckabee. I've gardened in Austin, Texas (zone 8b) since 1985. I garden with low maintenance, native and well-adapted non-native plants to conserve water and reduce workload. Here, you can read about my philosophy of gardening: why I believe it's important and responsible to incorporate native plants and water-wise practices in a wildlife attracting and regionally appropriate landscape.

feeds.title: Central Texas Gardener Blog
feeds.description: Central Texas Gardener is all about organic gardening, outstanding water wise plants, design inspiration, wildlife, homegrown food, and creative fun in the garden. See how to tackle the techniques, pick drought-tough plants for wildlife, fill up your kitchen with fresh food, and enrich your soul with artistic designs and homegrown philosophy from hands-on gardeners.

feeds.title: The Woodlands Township Environmental » Gardening and Landscaping
feeds.description: Posts about Gardening and Landscaping written by Environmental Services. The Woodlands Township Environmental Services Department coordinates a wide variety of programs that provide information and resources for healthy, sustainable living.

feeds.title: Red Wheelbarrow Blog
feeds.description: Colleen loves helping DO-IT-YOURSELFERS figure out what to do with their yards. Since founding Red Wheelbarrow over fifteen years ago she's helped transform hundreds of yards in Central Texas. As a top gardening educator, she is often asked to speak to audiences about native Texas planting.

feeds.title: Counting Tomatoes
feeds.description: A blog foused on gardening, growing fresh fruits and vegetables on the homestead, in addition to, recipes from scratch, money saving tips and DIY Projects.

feeds.title: Dian Farmer
feeds.description: Dian, an enthusiastic gardener, invites you to join her on her journey to cultivate food for her family and others. Through this blog, she shares her passion for helping people and imparts the gardening tips, tricks, and knowledge she's gleaned through her own experiences and continuous learning.

feeds.title: Buchanan's Native Plants Blog
feeds.description: Buchanan's Native Plants has been serving Houston gardeners since 1986. Located in historic Houston Heights, the garden center is dedicated to native plants and organic gardening. You will find the best selections of hardy natives as well as perennials, herbs, vegetables, trees, shrubs & roses - all suited to the Houston climate. The blog provides valuable tips, suggestions, and a forum to share ideas about getting the most from your garden.

feeds.title: Rooted Garden Blog
feeds.description: Learn to grow an organic raised bed kitchen garden in Houston Texas from the experts at Rooted Garden. Tour some of our most beautiful raised garden bed creations and learn more about organic vegetable gardening in and around Houston. All of us at Rooted Garden harvest delicious food from our gardens every single week of the year.

feeds.title: Coppell Community Garden
feeds.description: Coppell Community Garden cultivates a healthy community where gardeners can enjoy gardening, learn about organic gardens, and share with the food pantry.

feeds.title: Austin Organic Gardeners Blog
feeds.description: Since 1945, our members have shared information about successfully raising vegetables and ornamentals without using harsh fertilizers and toxic pesticides that harm the soil and disturb the ecological balance. We are the oldest organic gardening club in the U.S. as recognized by Rodale Institute and in 2020 during the pandemic, we celebrated 75 years as a club.

feeds.title: Plants for All Seasons Blog
feeds.description: Whether you are a beginner gardener or a master gardener, you can always learn something new from the Plants for All Seasons blog. We are a retail garden center, and have been 'getting our green on' since 1973 in the Houston area.

feeds.title: Garden Style San Antonio » Garden
feeds.description: Our resident expert The Garden Geek is here to help!Mark A. Peterson is a conservation project coordinator for San Antonio Water System. With more than 30 years of experience as an urban forester and arborist, Mark is probably the only person you know who actually prunes trees for fun. When not expounding on the benefits of trees and limited lawns, you're likely to find him hiking San Antonio's wilderness parks or extolling the virtues of geography and history to his friends.

feeds.title: North Haven Gardens Blog
feeds.description: Follow the North Haven Gardens blog to learn about gardening in the state of Texas and build yourself a lively garden. North Haven Gardens has a rich history here in Dallas. In 1951, Ralph and Muriel Pinkus founded NHG as a small nursery on nine acres of grassland along Northaven Rd. north of Dallas. They began with landscaping but quickly included selling retail plants to anyone who would make the drive. With a commitment to quality and value for their customers, the nursery has grown into one of the most respected horticultural ventures in the area.

feeds.title: Two Hoes Gardening Blog
feeds.description: Two Hoes Gardening blog: education, tips, insights, and connection. Building relationships through intentional gardening. We're just two San Antonio moms who love plants and teaching people how to grow successful gardens. Inspired by the educational and environmental benefits of gardening, we are passionate about making San Antonio greener one garden at a time.
